name: Espresso
shortDescription: A concentrated drink made by forcing hot water through ground coffee.
fullDescription: Espresso is the base of most drinks on a coffee-shop menu. A small serving has a rich flavor, a dense body and a layer of foam called crema. It is drunk on its own or used as the base for cappuccino, latte and other drinks.
historyAndCulture: Espresso originated in Italy. The first machines that brewed coffee with steam pressure appeared in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, and the drink became a symbol of Italian coffee culture: it is drunk quickly, often standing at the bar.
preparationMethod:
Grind the beans finely and tamp the coffee in the portafilter.
Start the extraction in the espresso machine and collect about 30 ml of drink.
Serve immediately while the crema lasts.

name: Americano
fullDescription: Americano is a longer and milder drink than espresso. You can change the amount of water depending on how strong you want it.
historyAndCulture: According to a popular legend, the name is linked to American soldiers in Italy who diluted espresso with water. The accuracy of this story is debated, so it is best treated as a legend.
preparationMethod:
Prepare the espresso.
Add hot water.
Serve immediately.

name: Cappuccino
shortDescription: Espresso with milk and milk foam.
fullDescription: Cappuccino combines espresso, hot milk and a layer of milk foam. The drink is known for a balanced taste in which coffee and milk blend harmoniously.
historyAndCulture: The name is usually linked to the color of the habits worn by Capuchin friars: the color of the drink resembles their robes. This explanation is often cited in coffee literature.
preparationMethod:
Prepare the espresso.
Froth the milk into a dense warm foam.
Slowly pour the milk into the espresso and spoon the foam on top.

name: Latte
shortDescription: Espresso with plenty of hot milk and a thin layer of foam.
fullDescription: Latte is a soft, gentle drink with much more milk than coffee. It is often served in a tall glass or a large cup.
historyAndCulture: The name comes from the Italian caffè latte, meaning "coffee with milk". In Italy the word latte on its own simply means "milk", so people there order a caffè latte.
preparationMethod:
Prepare the espresso.
Warm and lightly froth the milk.
Pour the milk into the espresso, leaving a thin layer of foam on top.

name: Iced latte
shortDescription: A cold latte: espresso, cold milk and ice.
fullDescription: Iced latte is a refreshing version of latte served over ice. It is easy to adapt: add a syrup or choose a plant-based milk.
preparationMethod:
Fill a glass with ice.
Pour in the cold milk.
Add the espresso and, if you like, a syrup. Stir gently.

name: Mocha
shortDescription: Espresso with chocolate and hot milk.
fullDescription: Mocha combines coffee, chocolate and milk. It is a sweeter, more dessert-like drink than a regular latte.
historyAndCulture: The name is linked to the port city of Mocha in Yemen, historically an important hub of the coffee trade.
preparationMethod:
Melt the chocolate in hot milk.
Prepare the espresso.
Combine the chocolate milk with the espresso.

name: Affogato
shortDescription: A scoop of ice cream topped with hot espresso.
fullDescription: Affogato is a simple dessert drink built on the contrast of hot and cold. Serve it immediately, before the ice cream melts.
historyAndCulture: The name comes from the Italian word affogato, meaning "drowned": the ice cream seems to drown in the espresso.
preparationMethod:
Put a scoop of vanilla ice cream in a glass or cup.
Prepare the espresso.
Pour the espresso over the ice cream and serve immediately.
